standard_prerequisites.use: Is the criterion used in both directions of the argument.

core_obligations: Record that part (2) is immediate from the Ext characterisation of derived completeness and the definitions (proof lines 26078-26079).

For part (1), let M -> N be a map of derived complete modules and K = (M -> N) the corresponding object of D(A); for f in I use that Ext^n_A(A_f, M) and Ext^n_A(A_f, N) vanish for all n to conclude that Ext^n_A(A_f, K) vanishes for all n, hence that K is derived complete (proof lines 26080-26085).
Use part (2) to conclude that Ker(M -> N) and Coker(M -> N) are objects of C (proof lines 26085-26086).

For a short exact sequence 0 -> M_1 -> M_2 -> M_3 -> 0 of A-modules with M_1 and M_3 derived complete, use the long exact sequence of Ext to conclude that M_2 is derived complete (proof lines 26087-26090).
Conclude that C is a weak Serre subcategory of the category of A-modules by the characterisation of weak Serre subcategories (proof lines 26091-26092).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I of a ring A and asserts two things: that the derived complete A-modules form a weak Serre subcategory C of the category of A-modules, and that the full subcategory spelled with C of D(A) is exactly the full subcategory of derived complete objects (source lines 26067-26076). Part (2) is immediate from the Ext characterisation of derived completeness and the definitions (proof lines 26078-26079). Part (1) is the substantive verification of the weak Serre axioms. First, for a map M -> N of derived complete modules with K the corresponding object of D(A), the proof uses that Ext^n_A(A_f, M) and Ext^n_A(A_f, N) vanish for all n and every f in I to conclude that Ext^n_A(A_f, K) vanishes for all n, hence that K is derived complete; then part (2) shows that the kernel and cokernel of M -> N lie in C (proof lines 26080-26086). Second, for a short exact sequence 0 -> M_1 -> M_2 -> M_3 -> 0 with M_1 and M_3 derived complete, the long exact sequence of Ext shows that M_2 is derived complete (proof lines 26087-26090). The conclusion that C is a weak Serre subcategory follows from the characterisation of weak Serre subcategories (proof lines 26091-26092). The non-routine content is the arrangement of the long exact Ext sequences so that the two weak Serre axioms are satisfied.
